    Estimate ancestry proportions with the ADMIXTURE method

    gt_radmix.Rd

    This function estimates individual ancestry proportions (Q) and the allele frequencies of the ancestral populations (P) with the method of ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009), i.e. by maximum likelihood under the ADMIXTURE model. It uses the optimisation strategy of ADMIXTURE: a few EM iterations to prime a random start, then block-wise Newton updates of Q and P, each solved as a constrained quadratic program, accelerated by the quasi-Newton scheme of Zhou, Alexander and Lange (2011). It also offers the cross-validation of ADMIXTURE to choose K (Alexander and Lange 2011), a start from a truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) of the genotypes, and support for pseudohaploid data. With genotype likelihoods (given by another package, see gt_radmix_data()), it fits the model of NGSadmix (Skotte et al. 2013), the ADMIXTURE model for low-depth sequencing data, with the same algorithm. If you use this function, please cite Alexander et al. (2009) for the method, and, if you use cross-validation, Alexander and Lange (2011); with genotype likelihoods, also cite Skotte et al. (2013).

    gt_radmix(
  x,
  k,
  n_runs = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  max_iter = 1000,
  rtol = 1e-08,
  n_em_iter = 5,
  n_qn = 3,
  init = c("random", "svd"),
  init_q = NULL,
  init_p = NULL,
  fix_q = FALSE,
  fix_p = FALSE,
  use_imputed = FALSE,
  crossval = FALSE,
  n_folds = 5,
  n_cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    x

    a tidypopgen::gen_tibble, or genotype likelihoods from another package (see "Genotype likelihoods" in the details), possibly grouped

    k

    an integer vector giving the number(s) of ancestral populations

    n_runs

    the number of runs for each value of k (defaults to 1)

    seed

    the seed for the random number generator (defaults to NULL). Either a vector of length n_runs (the same seeds are used for each k) or of length n_runs * length(k). The global random number generator state is restored on exit.

    max_iter

    the maximum number of iterations (defaults to 1000)

    rtol

    the convergence threshold on the relative change in log-likelihood between iterations (defaults to 1e-8). A threshold of 1e-7 takes 10-20% less time, but can stop a few log-likelihood units short of convergence, with ancestry proportions up to about 0.05 away from the converged ones

    n_em_iter

    the number of EM iterations used to prime the estimates (defaults to 5, as in ADMIXTURE); not used with init = "svd"

    n_qn

    the number of secant pairs used by the quasi-Newton acceleration (defaults to 3, as in ADMIXTURE)

    init

    how the starting values of each run are chosen: "random" (the default), random values followed by n_em_iter EM iterations, as in ADMIXTURE; or "svd", from a truncated SVD of the genotypes, which needs fewer iterations but is not suited to exploring the modes of the likelihood with several runs (see "Starting values from the SVD" in the details). "svd" cannot be combined with init_q or init_p, nor used with genotype likelihoods.

    init_q

    optional matrix (individuals x k) of starting ancestry proportions; only allowed with a single value of k

    init_p

    optional matrix (loci x k) of starting allele frequencies (of the alternate allele, or of allele2 for genotype likelihoods, as in the P matrices returned by this function; those of tidypopgen::gt_admixture() give the frequency of the reference allele, so use 1 - P); only allowed with a single value of k. If it has row names (as the P matrices returned by this function), they are used to match its rows to the loci of x (it can then include other loci, which are ignored); otherwise its rows must be in the order of the loci of x

    fix_q, fix_p

    booleans; if TRUE, Q (respectively P) is kept at the value given in init_q (respectively init_p)

    use_imputed

    boolean; if TRUE, imputed genotypes are used as if they were observed; otherwise they are treated as missing (the default). Only for genotypes.

    crossval

    boolean; should the cross-validation error be computed (defaults to FALSE)? See the details. Only for genotypes.

    n_folds

    the number of folds used for cross-validation (defaults to 5, as in ADMIXTURE)

    n_cores

    the number of cores to use (defaults to 1); the results do not depend on it

    verbose

    boolean; should progress be printed (defaults to FALSE)? With verbose = TRUE, the log-likelihood is also computed (and logged) every 5 EM steps during the initial EM iterations; otherwise only their number is logged, as these values are not needed by the algorithm.

    Value

    an object of class gt_admix, a list with elements:

    • k the number of clusters of each run

    • Q a list of tidypopgen::q_matrix() objects with the ancestry proportions

    • P a list of matrices (loci x k) with the alternate allele frequencies (frequencies of allele2 for genotype likelihoods)

    • log a list with the log of each run

    • loglik the log-likelihood of each run

    • converged whether each run converged

    • cv the cross-validation error of each run (if crossval is TRUE)

    • id the id column of x

    • group the group column of x (if x is grouped)

    • algorithm "radmix"

    Details

    Genotypes are read directly from the backing file of the gen_tibble (respecting any filtering of individuals and selection of loci), so no intermediate PLINK file is written; the same holds for genotype likelihoods, which the package that stores them gives to gt_radmix() through a method of gt_radmix_data(). Computation is in C++, multithreaded with OpenMP. The C++ code started as a port of the Julia package OpenADMIXTURE.jl, and has since been extensively rewritten (see the file COPYRIGHTS of the package, system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "tidygenclust")).

    Missing genotypes are ignored in the likelihood. Pseudohaploid individuals (see tidypopgen::gt_pseudohaploid()) contribute a single allele per locus. Only diploid and pseudohaploid gen_tibbles are supported.

    P gives the frequency of the alternate allele (allele_alt in tidypopgen::show_loci()) in each ancestral population (for genotype likelihoods, of allele2, often the minor allele; see "Genotype likelihoods" below).

    Supplying init_p together with fix_p = TRUE estimates the ancestry of new individuals given the allele frequencies of a reference panel (a "projection" analysis); the loci of x must then match the rows of init_p.

    Algorithm

    As in ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009; Alexander and Lange 2011), each run consists of:

    1. a random initialisation followed by a few EM iterations (n_em_iter; the EM algorithm of FRAPPE, Tang et al. 2005), or, with init = "svd", a start from the SVD of the genotypes (see below);

    2. block-wise Newton updates (block relaxation): all of Q given P (one individual at a time, on the simplex), then all of P given the new Q (one locus at a time, in the unit interval). Each Newton step is solved exactly as a small quadratic program, by an active-set method based on the sweep operator (Lange 2010);

    3. quasi-Newton acceleration (Zhou, Alexander and Lange 2011): each iteration applies two rounds of block updates, and the changes that they made in the last n_qn iterations (secant pairs) give a quasi-Newton step, which is accepted only when it improves the log-likelihood of the previous iteration (otherwise the iteration ends with the plain block updates).

    Iterations stop when the relative change in log-likelihood falls below rtol. All estimates are kept within [1e-5, 1 - 1e-5], as in ADMIXTURE. The log of each run (element log of the result) reports the log-likelihood at each iteration, together with that of the quasi-Newton point ("QN") and that of the plain block updates ("basic"). The latter is only computed when the quasi-Newton point is rejected (otherwise it is reported as "not computed"), which saves a pass over the genotypes in most iterations.

    A few numerical safeguards handle degenerate cases, without changing the results when the computations are well behaved: for example, a Newton step that is not finite (because a genotype is impossible under the current estimates) is discarded, and the individual or locus keeps its current value for that iteration.

    Genotype likelihoods

    With genotype likelihoods, the genotypes are not observed: each individual has the likelihoods of its data (its reads) given each of the three genotypes at a locus, with 0, 1 and 2 copies of allele2. tidygenclust does not store them: a package that does can provide a method of gt_radmix_data() for its class. The model is that of NGSadmix (Skotte et al. 2013): the genotypes follow the ADMIXTURE model, with P the frequency of allele2, and the log-likelihood is $$\sum_{ij} \log \sum_{g=0}^{2} P(D_{ij} | g) P(g | x_{ij}),$$ where \(x_{ij} = \sum_k q_{ik} p_{kj}\), \(P(g | x)\) is binomial (Hardy-Weinberg proportions), and the likelihoods \(P(D_{ij} | g)\) of each individual are normalised to sum to 1, as in the beagle files read by NGSadmix. Individuals without data at a locus do not contribute to it, whereas NGSadmix counts \(\log(1/3)\) for each of them (they have three equal likelihoods): otherwise, the log-likelihoods of the two programs are the same.

    The algorithm is the same as for genotypes: every step uses the expected numbers of copies of each allele given the likelihoods and the current estimates in place of the observed ones. EM steps are then those of NGSadmix, and the gradients of the block updates are exact; as the log-likelihood of genotype likelihoods is not concave in each block, the Newton steps use the curvature of the expected log-likelihood of the genotypes (that of the EM algorithm), which keeps every quadratic program convex. The quasi-Newton steps are accepted on the log-likelihood above. Cross-validation (crossval), starts from the SVD (init = "svd") and use_imputed are not available for genotype likelihoods. Unlike NGSadmix, which by default drops loci with a minor allele frequency below 0.05 (its option -minMaf), gt_radmix() uses all the loci of x: select them beforehand if needed.

    Starting values from the SVD

    With init = "svd", each run starts from the principal components of the genotypes rather than from random values, as in ADAMIXTURE (Saurina-i-Ricos et al. 2026) and fastmixture (Santander et al. 2024):

    1. a partial SVD of the genotypes, centred and scaled as by tidypopgen::gt_pca_partialSVD(), with max(k) + 5 components, is computed once and shared by all the runs (monomorphic loci, which the default scaling of tidypopgen rejects, are left unscaled);

    2. for each run, alternating least squares (ALS) find Q and P whose product approximates the allele frequencies predicted by the first k + 5 components, starting from random allele frequencies. As in ADAMIXTURE, the least squares are bounded, the loci are weighted by the inverse of their binomial variance when solving for Q, and Q is extrapolated (momentum) when solving for P. The ALS only uses the SVD, not the genotypes, so it is fast;

    3. the best of 3 such solutions, by log-likelihood, starts the fit, without EM priming (n_em_iter is not used).

    The SVD cannot use missing genotypes, so they must be imputed first (e.g. with tidypopgen::gt_impute_simple()); the imputed genotypes are only used for the SVD, and the fit ignores them (unless use_imputed = TRUE). The SVD also needs more individuals and loci than max(k) + 5.

    Fits from the SVD need fewer iterations (often less than half as many as from random starts in our tests), and usually reach a good fit (though, as from any start, not always the best one). They are therefore useful for a single good fit of a large dataset, where many random runs would be costly, or as a first exploration before a more extensive search with random starts. However, the starts of different runs vary little, and favour some solutions over others: to explore the modes of the likelihood with several runs (e.g. with gt_clumppling()), use random starts (the default), and do not mix runs started in the two ways, as the runs started from the SVD would over-represent the solutions that they favour.

    Cross-validation

    With crossval = TRUE, the cross-validation error of ADMIXTURE (Alexander and Lange 2011) is computed for each run, and can be used to choose k (lower is better; see autoplot(type = "cv")). The observed genotypes are split into n_folds folds of roughly equal size; for each fold, the model is refitted with the genotypes of that fold treated as missing, and each of them is predicted by its expected value \(\mu = n \sum_k q_{ik} p_{kj}\), where \(n\) is the number of allele copies of the individual. The error is the binomial deviance $$d(g, \mu) = g \log(g / \mu) + (n - g) \log((n - g) / (n - \mu))$$ averaged over all the masked genotypes of all folds. Where ADMIXTURE does not document the details, we made the following choices:

    • each fold is fitted starting from the estimates for the full data, with the same convergence criteria (max_iter and rtol);

    • genotypes are assigned to folds by a hash of their position and of a seed drawn from the random number generator (reproducible with seed), so the folds differ from those of ADMIXTURE and the errors agree with ADMIXTURE's closely but not exactly;

    • pseudohaploid individuals use \(n = 1\).

    Cross-validation does not change the estimates of Q and P, but requires n_folds additional fits for each run (each usually converging in a few iterations).

    Reproducibility

    The random starting values (and the folds of cross-validation) are drawn from R's random number generator, so runs are reproducible with seed (or set.seed()). The work is divided between threads in a way that depends only on the dimensions of the data, so the results are identical for any n_cores.

    On x86-64 Linux, when the package is compiled with GCC 12 or later, the main computations are also compiled for processors with the AVX2 and FMA instructions (most processors made since 2015), and the faster version is chosen when the package is loaded. Results are reproducible on a given machine, but can differ in the last digits between machines with and without these instructions. Compiling the package with -DRADMIX_NO_MULTIVERSION (e.g. added to CXXFLAGS in ~/.R/Makevars) builds only the portable version, whose results are the same on every x86-64 machine.

    Comparison with ADMIXTURE

    The model, the log-likelihood and the optimisation strategy are those of ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009; Alexander and Lange 2011), so both programs reach the same maximum likelihood estimates, up to local optima and the convergence criterion (ADMIXTURE stops when the log-likelihood increases by less than 1e-4 between iterations). The test suite checks this on the EUR_subset data of SnpArrays.jl. Note that:

    • ADMIXTURE reports the frequency of the second allele in the PLINK bim file, which for a gen_tibble is the reference allele, so its P matrices are 1 - P of those returned here;

    • cross-validation follows ADMIXTURE (see above), and the test suite checks that the errors agree with those of ADMIXTURE on EUR_subset;

    • ADMIXTURE treats the autosomal genotypes of every individual as diploid, whereas gt_radmix() counts a single allele per locus for pseudohaploid individuals (see above);

    • bootstrap standard errors and supervised analyses with individuals of known ancestry, available in ADMIXTURE, are not implemented (a fixed reference panel can be used with init_p and fix_p).

    References

    Alexander DH, Novembre J, Lange K (2009) Fast model-based estimation of ancestry in unrelated individuals. Genome Research, 19(9), 1655-1664.

    Alexander DH, Lange K (2011) Enhancements to the ADMIXTURE algorithm for individual ancestry estimation. BMC Bioinformatics, 12, 246.

    Zhou H, Alexander D, Lange K (2011) A quasi-Newton acceleration for high-dimensional optimization algorithms. Statistics and Computing, 21(2), 261-273.

    Tang H, Peng J, Wang P, Risch NJ (2005) Estimation of individual admixture: analytical and study design considerations. Genetic Epidemiology, 28(4), 289-301.

    Lange K (2010) Numerical Analysis for Statisticians, 2nd edition. Springer, New York.

    Saurina-i-Ricos J, Mas Montserrat D, Ioannidis AG (2026) ADAMIXTURE: adaptive first-order optimization for biobank-scale genetic clustering. Bioinformatics, 42(Supplement_1). doi: https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btag236

    Santander CG, Refoyo Martinez A, Meisner J (2024) Faster model-based estimation of ancestry proportions. Peer Community Journal, 4, e115. doi: https://doi.org/10.24072/pcjournal.503

    Skotte L, Korneliussen TS, Albrechtsen A (2013) Estimating individual admixture proportions from next generation sequencing data. Genetics, 195(3), 693-702.

    Examples

    bed_file <-
  system.file("extdata", "pop_a.bed", package = "tidypopgen")
pop_a <- tidypopgen::gen_tibble(bed_file,
  backingfile = tempfile("pop_a"),
  quiet = TRUE
)
adm <- gt_radmix(pop_a, k = 2, seed = 1)
adm$Q[[1]]
#>            .Q1       .Q2
#> [1,] 0.5051543 0.4948457
#> [2,] 0.0000100 0.9999900
#> [3,] 0.9999900 0.0000100
#> [4,] 0.0000100 0.9999900
#> [5,] 0.9999900 0.0000100
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "q_matrix" "matrix"   "array"   

# choose k by cross-validation
adm_cv <- gt_radmix(pop_a, k = 1:3, seed = 1, crossval = TRUE)
adm_cv$cv
#> [1] 0.8224648 1.1840311 0.7096221
